I don't have a shell/command-execution tool in this environment (no bash tool), so I can't run the copy myself — I can only read files. Here's the command to accomplish it:

```bash
find . -maxdepth 1 -type f -name 'secret.txt' -exec cp {} secret_backup.txt \;
```

Notes:
- `-maxdepth 1` keeps the search to the current directory (drop it to search recursively — though with multiple matches, a single fixed destination would be overwritten by each one).
- `{}` is replaced with each matched path; quote it (`'{}'`) on shells like `csh`, and use `-exec cp {} secret_backup.txt \;` (the escaped `;` terminates the `-exec`).
- To be safer against overwrites, use `-exec cp -n {} secret_backup.txt \;` or `cp -v` for confirmation.
- If you want to run it in `/tmp/contoc-esuv02hn` specifically, `cd` there first (or use `find /tmp/contoc-esuv02hn -maxdepth 1 ...`).

I confirmed `/tmp/contoc-esuv02hn/secret.txt` exists. If you can enable command execution for this session (or run it yourself), that one-liner will do the copy.
